title: Evolution of Heuristics: Towards Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design Using Large Language Model
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning

publication.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-based evolution of combinatorial optimization heuristics
mechanism.populationDetail: Maintains a flat population of N heuristic individuals, each represented by natural-language thought, executable code, and fitness.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; fitness-ranked survivors form the next population.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Up to 5N feasible offspring are incrementally added to the current pool, after which the top N individuals are selected as the next generation.
mechanism.generationDetail: Initialization is from scratch; E1/E2 generate using multiple selected parents (E2 explicitly synthesizes their common idea), while M1/M2/M3 modify one parent heuristic.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Fitness aggregates task performance over instances and drives rank-biased parent sampling and top-N survivor selection.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Experiments rank the current population by fitness and sample individual i with probability proportional to 1/(\(rank_i\)+N). E1/E2 use \(p=5\) parents in the online bin-packing setup; M1-M3 use one.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The evolved individual is a coupled dual representation: a natural-language thought and executable heuristic code are co-evolved and jointly evaluated.

provenance.citationWarning: EoH is genuinely hybrid across multi-parent E1/E2 and unary M1-M3 operators; E1/E2 parent count is p=5 in the reported bin-packing setting, while M operators use one. The paper calls E strategies exploration and M strategies modification, so mapping M to exploitation is a survey-level interpretation. Fitness-ranked survivor selection is generational, not a separate elite archive.
